scope: Local behavioral reinforcement of the existing GALX Star and image workflow under the institutional selection mandate; no interface redesign or live release.
findings: The pass preserves the existing navigation, feed, cards, profile, collections and studio layout. No new application, dashboard, navigation shell or creation surface was added.

Public feed/profile DTOs, search, saved-work normalization and exports no longer expose production prompts or unmetered remix counters. Existing owner-authorized private work remains available through its private library contract; legacy locally cached public prompts are removed during normalization.

A private remix request carries a published Star work ID and the patron's direction. The server validates the current public Star source and composes the private prompt context. The existing authenticated purchased-allowance pipeline owns admission; the result remains a private human Work.

New Star outputs remain private candidates. The internal reviewer records an append-only selection/withholding decision for the exact asset set, with rationale, reviewer and increasing decision version. Database constraints recheck completed attempt, actor, asset provenance and selection before public visibility is committed. Direct visibility writes cannot promote a candidate; previously published Star Works retain their state.

Generation success does not update artistic canon or imply exhibition. The selection command is an internal CLI with sanitized local previews; no public publication route or patron-to-Star path exists.

BROC practice history orders events by an identity sequence so equal timestamps do not change retrieved context order. Partial indexes and latest-row queries bound candidate and decision lookups as history grows. Practice remains private and append-only; pixel-level critique and automatic canon promotion are outside this implementation.

The impact report's unmapped paths were inspected: they are private current-state/release evidence and the self-referential critical/domain review records, not untracked product or implementation boundaries. New selection code, tests and ADR are mapped to their owning domains.

focused_checks.documentation: PASS: npm run docs:sync, npm run docs:check (377 guides, 41 incident documents, 163 ADRs and 10 reviewed domains), npm run test:docs (24 incident tests and 17 knowledge tests), and git diff --check.

production_changes: NONE in this pass. No shared database migration, application deployment, provider generation, allowance mutation or Premium runtime change occurred. The existing local Premium queue deployment remains separately documented.
limits: Both new migrations remain local and unapplied. Public candidate-selection behavior is not hosted or production-accepted.
The private candidate review CLI is an operator tool and was not exercised against shared production data.
The scan covers this local build and its 526 enumerated rendered/browser assets; it does not establish that any deployed site is clean.
Previously downloaded public prompts or artifacts cannot be recalled by changing current serializers. No historical execution record was deleted.
